 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In addition to the facility fee (2.5% of $300.0 million) paid in connection with the commitment and the
closing of the Senior Finance Facility and an anniversary fee of 1.5% due on the anniversary of the initial borrowing, the Company issued a warrant exercisable for 1,190,148 shares of the Company&#146;s common stock at an exercise price of $15.25
per share (the deemed value of the shares), subject to adjustment under certain anti-dilution provisions of the warrant and agreed to pay an unused commitment fee of 0.25%&nbsp;per annum on the excess availability under the Senior Finance Facility.
The $8.7 million value of the warrant issued to the Senior Finance Facility lender was determined using a Black-Scholes model based on a risk-free interest rate of 3.81%, expected volatility of 50% and an expected life of 5 years. The February 2004
amendment reduced the exercise price of warrants to purchase 1,190,148 shares of the Company&#146;s common stock from $15.25 per share to $14.00 per share and also required the Company to pay Merrill Lynch Mortgage Capital, Inc. a commission equal
to 1.5% of Vacation Interest revenue on the sale of inventory acquired from Epic Resorts Group. As a result of the February 2004 amendment, an additional $0.4 million was recorded to reflect the decrease in exercise price. The value of the warrant
was recorded as a capitalized financing cost that is amortized over the term of the financing agreement. The February 2004 amendment also stipulated that facility fees equal to 0.75% of $300.0 million were due and payable on July&nbsp;29, 2004 and
July&nbsp;29, 2005, with the latter fee being prorated through the then termination date of February&nbsp;28, 2006. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">For the year ended September&nbsp;30, 2005, the nine months ended September&nbsp;30, 2004, and the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2003, amortization of $4.2
million, $5.5 million and $10.8 million, respectively, of debt issuance costs related to the Senior Finance Facility is included in interest expense in the accompanying consolidated statements of operations. The Senior Finance Facility also requires
the Company to pay an additional cash interest amount monthly when certain conditions are not met. The total amount of such additional cash interest payments made during the year ended September&nbsp;30, 2005, the nine months ended
September&nbsp;30, 2004, and the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2003 was $0.0 million, $0.3 million and $2.2 million, respectively. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">At September&nbsp;30, 2005, the maximum capacity to borrow, amounts outstanding, and remaining availability under the Senior Finance Facility were $300.0
million, $198.8 million and $101.2 million, respectively. The capacity and availability of borrowings under the Senior Finance Facility are based on the value of eligible mortgages and contracts receivable and the value of eligible unsold Vacation
Interests. The Senior Finance Facility is secured by a first priority lien on the mortgages and contracts receivable and unsold Vacation Interests. The weighted average interest rate of these borrowings at September&nbsp;30, 2005 was 5.8%&nbsp;per
annum. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Company&#146;s Senior Finance Facility contains
various restrictions and limitations that may affect its business and affairs. These include restrictions and limitations relating to its ability to incur indebtedness and other obligations, to make investments and acquisitions and to pay dividends.
This facility also requires the Company to maintain certain financial ratios and comply with other financial covenants. The failure of the Company to comply with any of these provisions, or to pay its obligations under the Senior Finance Facility or
other loan agreements, could result in foreclosure by the lenders of their security interests in the Company&#146;s assets, and could otherwise have a material adverse effect on the Company. </FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Company has capitalized interest related to ongoing construction projects
of $0.5 million for the year ended September&nbsp;30, 2005, $0.2 million and for the nine months ended September&nbsp;30, 2004, and $0.4 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2003. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Senior Subordinated Convertible Notes </I></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT
SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">On March&nbsp;29, 2004, the Company issued $95.0 million in 3<FONT SIZE="1"><SUP>&nbsp;3</SUP></FONT><FONT
SIZE="2">/</FONT><FONT SIZE="1">4</FONT><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2" COLOR="#000000">% Senior Subordinated Convertible Notes due 2024 (the &#147;Notes&#148;). The Notes were issued at a price of $1,000 per Note and pay interest
semi-annually on March&nbsp;29 and September&nbsp;29 of each year, beginning on September&nbsp;29, 2004 at the rate of 3.75%&nbsp;per annum. The Notes will mature on March&nbsp;29, 2024. Under the terms of the indenture, the Company was required to
use a portion of the proceeds from the offering to purchase a portfolio of U.S. government securities that are pledged to secure the first six scheduled interest payments on the Notes. This $10.4 million was recorded in Prepaid expenses and other
assets, net, and the balance on the accompanying balance sheets as of September&nbsp;30, 2005 and 2004 was $5.3 million and $8.7 million, respectively. Other than this pledge, the Notes are unsecured obligations. </FONT></FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Notes are convertible, at the option of the holder, into shares of the
Company&#146;s common stock at a conversion rate of 62.5027 shares per $1,000 principal amount of the Notes once: the price of the Company&#146;s common stock is more than 110% of such implied conversion price of $16.00 per common share for more
than 20 trading days during the last 30 trading days of a calendar quarter; the Notes are called for redemption; or specified corporate transactions or significant distributions to holders of the Company&#146;s common stock have occurred. In
addition, the Notes are convertible during the five business day period after any five consecutive trading day period ending on or prior to March&nbsp;29, 2019 in which the trading price per note for each day of that five trading day period was less
than 98% of the product of the sale price of the Company&#146;s common stock and the conversion rate on each such day. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Holders of the Notes may require the Company to purchase for cash all or a portion of their Notes on March&nbsp;29, 2011,&nbsp;March&nbsp;29, 2014 and on
March&nbsp;29, 2019 at a price equal to $1,000 per $1,000 principal amount of the Notes, plus accrued and unpaid interest, if any, to the date of the purchase. In addition, if the Company experiences a change in control, each holder may require the
Company to purchase all or a portion of such holder&#146;s Notes at the same amount, plus, in certain circumstances, a make-whole premium. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Company may redeem some or all of the Notes for cash at any time on or after March&nbsp;29, 2007, if the closing price of the Company&#146;s common
stock has exceeded 150% of the conversion price then in effect for at least 20 trading days within a period of 30 consecutive trading days ending on the trading day before the mailing date of the corresponding redemption notice. On or after
March&nbsp;29, 2011, the Company may redeem some or all of the Notes for cash at any time at a price of $1,000 per $1,000 principal amount of the Notes, plus accrued and unpaid interest, if any, to the redemption date. </FONT></P> <P

STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Securitization Notes </I></B></FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">On September&nbsp;30, 2004, the Company completed a $151.7 million private
offering and sale of vacation ownership receivable-backed notes (the &#147;2004 Securitization&#148;). The $171.4 million (including $17.0 million in aggregate principal of vacation ownership receivables sold during the ninety day period commencing
September&nbsp;30, 2004) in aggregate principal of vacation ownership receivables that collateralize the notes were initially sold to Sunterra SPE 2004-1 LLC (&#147;SPE 2004-1&#148;), a wholly-owned, special-purpose entity that deposited the
vacation ownership receivables into the Sunterra Owner Trust 2004-1, which issued the notes and is included within Sunterra Corporation&#146;s consolidated financial statements, without recourse to the Company or to SPE 2004-1, except for breaches
of certain representations and warranties at the time of sale. The 2004 Securitization is secured by a first priority lien on the mortgages and contracts receivable sold to Sunterra Owner Trust 2004-1. </FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">On October&nbsp;27, 2004 and December&nbsp;1, 2004, the Company completed
pre-funding transactions with the Sunterra Owner Trust 2004-1. On October&nbsp;27, 2004, $11.1 million in vacation ownership receivables were sold to Sunterra Owner Trust 2004-1 and on December&nbsp;1, 2004, $5.9 million of vacation ownership
receivables were sold to Sunterra Owner Trust 2004-1. As a result of these two transactions, the $17.0 million classified as restricted cash as of September&nbsp;30, 2004 was released ratably on these two dates and transferred to the Company in
exchange for these vacation ownership receivables. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The $151.7
million private offering consists of: $66.0 million class A notes &#145;AAA&#146;, $18.4 million class B notes &#145;AA&#146;, $17.6 million class C notes &#145;A&#146; and $49.7 million class D notes &#145;BBB&#146;. The notes carry various fixed
interest rates ranging from 3.6% to 4.9% and have legal stated maturities of October 2020. The actual maturity of the notes could be significantly earlier than the stated maturity, and the average life of the notes could be significantly shorter
than anticipated, in the event of certain occurrences. Interest and principal payments are due monthly. In addition, the notes contain a &#147;clean up&#148; call provision that allows the notes to be called and mortgages receivable to be
transferred back to the Company when the remaining principal value of the notes reaches 10% of the original principal value. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Under the terms of the indenture, Sunterra Financial Services, Inc., a direct wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company, in exchange for a monthly fee,
services and administers the vacation ownership receivables in Sunterra Owner Trust 2004-1. All monthly fees are eliminated as part of the Company&#146;s consolidation of the Sunterra Owner Trust 2004-1. </FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The proceeds were used to pay down balances due under the Company&#146;s
Senior Finance Facility, pay fees associated with the transaction to third parties and deposit initial amounts in a required cash reserve account. The Company also retained a subordinated interest in the future cash flows from the 2004
Securitization. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">For the year ended September&nbsp;30, 2005,

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Note 12&#151;Employee Benefit Plans </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT
SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Company has established a qualified retirement plan (the &#147;401(k) Plan&#148;), with a salary deferral feature
designed to qualify under Section&nbsp;401 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended. Subject to certain limitations, the 401(k) Plan allows participating employees to defer up to 15% of their eligible compensation on a pre-tax basis. The
401(k) Plan allows the Company to make discretionary matching contributions of up to 50% of employee contributions, though no such matching contributions were made during the nine months ended September&nbsp;30, 2004 or the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2003. During the year ended September&nbsp;30, 2005, the Company made matching contributions of $.06 million. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Company has a self-insured health plan which covers substantially all of its full time employees in the United States. The health plan uses employee
and employer contributions to pay eligible claims. To supplement the plan, the Company has stop-loss insurance to cover individual claims in excess of $0.2 million. The Company has accrued for claims that have been incurred but not reported.
</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Effective October&nbsp;11, 2000, the Company implemented an
employee retention plan for certain management and other key employees. The purpose of the plan was to encourage these employees to continue their employment with the Company during the Chapter 11 proceedings. The plan provided up to $3.0 million in
retention bonuses for employees covered by the plan, subject to continued employment and the plan&#146;s eligibility and vesting requirements. Effective August&nbsp;21, 2001, the Company amended its key employee retention plan. The Company paid $1.0
million in bonuses under the retention plan during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2003. No amounts have been paid under the retention plan subsequent to 2003. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Provision has not been made for taxes on approximately $46.6 million and $48.9 million of undistributed
earnings of foreign subsidiaries as of September&nbsp;30, 2005 and 2004, respectively. Those earnings have been and expect to be reinvested in the foreign subsidiaries. The American Jobs Creation Act of 2004 provides a special provision whereby
United States taxpayers could have foreign earnings repatriated and receive a dividends received deduction of 85%. As of the filing of the financial statements, the Company has not completed its evaluation to determine if any foreign earnings would
be repatriated, and expects to complete its evaluation before the end of the period in which repatriation of foreign earnings can take place. The Company is not in a position to provide an estimate of the amount that would be considered for
repatriation. In the event that the earnings are repatriated, the Company may have to provide additional tax expense, net of foreign tax credits. Further, these earnings could become subject to additional tax if the Company were to sell its stock in
the subsidiaries. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Note 14&#151;Related Party Transactions </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Delinquent Maintenance Fee Receivables Agreements </I></B></FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Effective January 2005, the Company entered into agreements with various
homeowners&#146; associations to purchase current year delinquent maintenance fee receivables from them at par value in North America. Such agreements contain provisions for the Company to utilize the Vacation Interests associated with such
maintenance fees in the current year and to reclaim such Vacation Interests in the future. Each such agreement provides for an initial June&nbsp;30 settlement date and adjustments thereafter. The Company&#146;s obligation under such agreements as of
the settlement date totaled approximately $5.4 million, including approximately $1.9 million related to current year use rights of the underlying Vacation Interests (expensed during calendar 2005 as a component of Vacation Interest carrying cost)
and approximately $3.5 million that will either be collected from the owners or remain on the Company&#146;s balance sheet as the cost basis of the reclaimed underlying Vacation Interests. In one of the homeowners&#146; association agreements, the
Company agreed to purchase other fees relating to special assessments. These special assessment fees are not yet delinquent, but the Company has the obligation to purchase any delinquent fees, which could range between $0.4 million and $0.9 million.
The amount of this obligation will be determined in the second quarter of fiscal 2006. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman"
SIZE="2"><B><I>Joint Ventures </I></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In August 2005, the
Company purchased the remaining 70% partnership interest in Poipu Resort Partners, L.P. (&#147;Poipu&#148;) and, in July 2004, purchased the remaining 77% partnership interest in West Maui Resort Partners, L.P. (&#147;Ka&#146;anapali&#148;) and, as
such, the Company is no longer a minority partner in any joint venture. For the year ended September&nbsp;30, 2005 and the nine months ended September&nbsp;30, 2004, the Company received $2.7 million and $3.2 million, respectively, in cash
distributions from Poipu. For the nine months ended September&nbsp;30, 2004, the Company received $0.5 million in cash distributions from Ka&#146;anapali. The Company also receives fees from both Poipu and Ka&#146;anapali for providing property
management as well as oversight of the sales and marketing functions, which are included in the totals for management services revenue. See &#147;Management Services&#148; paragraph below. </FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Management Services </I></B></FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Included within the amounts reported as management services revenue are
revenues from property management services provided to the homeowners&#146; associations of the resorts wherein the Company owns either unsold Vacation Interests or is a minority owner, as well as fees earned for management of sales and marketing
functions at certain resorts. These amounts totaled $19.7 million for the year ended September&nbsp;30, 2005, $15.5 million for the nine months ended September&nbsp;30, 2004 and $21.1 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2003. </FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Under contracts approved by the Boards of Trustees of the homeowners&#146;
association for certain resorts, the Company serves as the property manager for these resorts. Additionally, the Company has contractual agreements with the homeowners&#146; associations of certain resorts to provide telephone services to the
property. Accounts receivable due from the homeowners&#146; associations generally are for management fees and other operating and maintenance expenses. Amounts payable to homeowners&#146; associations, consisting primarily of maintenance fees for
unsold Vacation Interests, are included in accrued liabilities. The Company also periodically advanced funds to the joint venture entity in which the Company was a minority partner (see &#147;Joint Ventures&#148; paragraph above). The following

</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Purchase Obligations
</I></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Company has entered into various purchase
obligations totaling $30.2 million as of September&nbsp;30, 2005 primarily relating to construction commitments and information technology related items for fiscal 2006. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Litigation and Other </I></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In 1997 the Company purchased, for $3.5 million, a perpetual license to use certain computer software from RCI Technology Corp. (&#147;RCITC&#148;),
formerly known as Resort Computer Corporation. The RCITC software was later modified, and ultimately substantially re-written, to create the Company&#146;s former enterprise computer system (known as &#147;SWORD&#148;), which was used by the
Company&#146;s North American operations until, following the Company&#146;s emergence from bankruptcy, SWORD was replaced by the Company&#146;s present proprietary ATLAS computer system. In 2002, RCITC filed a motion in the Chapter 11 proceedings
alleging that the license agreement should be deemed rejected, which RCITC asserts would have the effect of terminating the license. The Company opposed the motion, and the Bankruptcy Court ruled in favor of Sunterra and denied RCITC&#146;s motion.
On January&nbsp;10, 2003, the United States District Court of Maryland affirmed the order of the Bankruptcy Court, denying the motion of RCITC. RCITC further appealed that decision to the United States Court of Appeals, Fourth Circuit, which granted
RCITC&#146;s appeal on March&nbsp;18, 2004. On remand, the Bankruptcy Court held on September&nbsp;8, 2005 that the RCITC license was deemed rejected as of July&nbsp;29, 2002, the date of the Company&#146;s emergence from bankruptcy. On
September&nbsp;22, 2005 the Company commenced a declaratory judgment action against RCITC in the United States District Court for the District of Colorado (Denver) seeking a declaration that, having paid the $3.5 million fee for a perpetual license
to the RCITC software, the &#147;rejection&#148; of that license did not terminate the Company&#146;s right to use the software, and that Sunterra&#146;s use of SWORD following July&nbsp;29, 2002 until it was replaced by ATLAS was not an
infringement of RCITC&#146;s copyright to the RCITC software. RCITC has answered the complaint, denying the Company&#146;s allegations, and asserting a counterclaim against Sunterra seeking a second payment of the $3.5 million license fee, as well
as additional damages. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">81 </FONT></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Company has answered RCITC&#146;s counterclaims, denying liability and asserting as a defense that the RCITC software
was defective. Discovery has not yet commenced in this litigation. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman"
SIZE="2">In 1997 and 1998 the Company entered into a series of agreements to acquire Vacation Internationale, a separate points-based vacation ownership club that was managed by the Company (under the name of Sunterra Pacific) until
December&nbsp;31, 2003. Under the terms of these agreements, the Company&#146;s subsidiary, Sunterra Pacific Inc., was required to transfer certain remainder interests in Vacation Internationale apartments to entities controlled by the founders of
Vacation Internationale (&#147;VI Founders&#148;). Over the years, many of these remainders were either purchased by the Company from the VI Founders, or were transferred to them pursuant to the terms of these agreements. However, for a variety of
reasons, transfer of the remainders for a Mexican resort, as well as a resort located on Native American land in Palm Springs, California, was delayed. In 2003, the VI Founders sued the Company and Sunterra Pacific in Washington State Court, King
County (Seattle), asserting various claims arising from the alleged breach by the Company and Sunterra Pacific of these agreements. The Company was later dismissed as a defendant and, during 2004, the case against Sunterra Pacific was stayed in
order for the parties to pursue settlement negotiations. Unless the stay is continued, the case is scheduled for trial commencing in April 2006. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In addition, the Company is also currently subject to litigation and claims regarding employment, tort, contract, construction, sales taxes and commission
disputes, among others. Much of such litigation and claims were pre-petition and were treated as general unsecured creditors under the Company&#146;s Plan of Reorganization. Management believes that none of these actions, including the actions
described above, will have a material adverse effect on the consolidated financial position or results of operations of the Company. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In October 2004, a standby letter of credit in the amount of $1.5 million was issued on the Company&#146;s behalf to Citrus Insurance Company, a
wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company. In March 2005, Citrus Insurance Company issued $7.7 million of surety bonds on behalf of other subsidiaries of the Company. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In addition to the surety bonds issued by Citrus Insurance Company, third-party financial institutions have issued surety
bonds totaling $6.3 million as of September&nbsp;30, 2005 on the Company&#146;s behalf to an affiliated homeowners&#146; association securing certain maintenance fee obligations due from the Company and for various other business purposes.
</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Company has entered into employment contracts with certain
key management employees that specify severance payments upon termination of the contracts. The employment contracts all specify stock compensation to be granted. See Note 9 for information regarding stock compensation due under these contracts.
</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Company&#146;s subsidiary in Europe has obtained a license
from the Civil Aviation Authority (the &#147;CAA&#148;) to operate as a tour operator through September 2006. Under the license with the CAA, the Company has agreed to limit repayment of advances between the Company and its subsidiary in Europe to
those amounts that have been outstanding less than one year, which approximates $6.4 million at September&nbsp;30, 2005, unless prior approval is received. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P

STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">SFAS No.&nbsp;107, <I>Disclosures about Fair Value of Financial Instruments</I>, requires that the Company disclose estimated fair values for its
financial instruments. The Company in estimating its fair value disclosures for financial instruments used the following methods and assumptions: </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P

necessary to fairly present the results of the quarterly financial information above, have been made. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Note 18&#151;Subsequent Events </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman"
SIZE="2">On October&nbsp;31, 2005, the Company sold a $35.0 million portfolio with a carrying value of approximately $32.5 million of mortgages receivable to Merrill Lynch Mortgage Lending, Inc., which resulted in a gain of approximately $3.0
million. Under the terms of the agreement, Merrill Lynch Mortgage Lending, Inc. paid $36.1 million in cash for a portfolio of $35 million of receivables secured by Vacation Interests at Sunterra properties. The sale was on a non-recourse basis and
the Company retained the right to service the receivables sold. The Company receives adequate compensation for providing the servicing functions. As such, no asset or liability will be recognized on the consolidated balance sheet for the servicing
rights retained. The pool of 5,250 receivables has a weighted-average seasoning of approximately four years and a weighted-average interest rate of 14.6%. Approximately 4,200 receivables representing $24 million of the receivables sold were either
originated by Epic Resort Group and subsequently purchased by Sunterra, or were included in Sunterra&#146;s former off-balance sheet pools repurchased by the Company in fiscal 2005. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">On December&nbsp;5, 2005, the Company acquired the land adjacent to the Misiones del Cabo Hotel and Resort property in Cabo
San Lucas, Mexico. The Company&#146;s site plan calls for three building phases. The total cost of the project at full build out will be approximately $50.0 million, which includes initial consideration of nearly $11.0 million for oceanfront land,
the related resort hospitality management contract, and construction deposits. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<A NAME="tx81132_14"></A>ITEM 9A. CONTROLS AND PROCEDURES </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman"
SIZE="2"><B><I>Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures </I></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Company&#146;s management, with the participation of the Company&#146;s Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, evaluated the effectiveness of the Company&#146;s disclosure controls and procedures as
of the end of the period covered by this report. Based on that evaluation, the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer concluded that the Company&#146;s disclosure controls and procedures as of the end of the period covered by this
report were designed and were functioning effectively to provide reasonable assurance that the information required to be disclosed by the Company in reports filed under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (i)&nbsp;is recorded, processed, summarized
and reported within the time periods specified in the SEC&#146;s rules and forms and (ii)&nbsp;accumulated and communicated to our management, including our chief executive officer and chief financial officer, as appropriate to allow timely
decisions regarding disclosure. The Company believes that a system of controls, no matter how well designed and operated, cannot provide absolute assurance that the objectives of the controls are met, and no evaluation of controls can provide
absolute assurance that all control issues and instances of fraud, if any, within a company have been detected. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Management&#146;s Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting </I></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT
